newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Wall St rise supports Euro stocks at peaks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wall St rise supports Euro stocks at peaks.

text.p: European shares held most of their earlier strong gains on Friday when Wall Street opened firmer on the back of the latest snapshot of the U.S. economy painting a picture of non-inflationary growth.
London shares were up 0.3 percent, while French and German shares were both up around one percent by 1400 gmt. All three made new trading records on the way up during the morning.
U.S. producer prices fell 0.3 percent in May, their fifth straight decline and making the first time the index has dropped five months in succession since 1952.

"This is very positive news on inflation which will probably be backed up (U.S.) consumer price figures next Tuesday," said Rob Hayward, economist at Bank of America in London, interviewed on Reuters Financial Television.
"But the big question that remains is whether the economy will continue to slow in the second half."

Wall Street's Dow Jones industrial index was up 25.33 points, or 0.3 percent, at 7,736.80 at 1400 gmt and rising, having stormed 135.64 higher on Thursday. The index closed above 7,500 for the first time only on Tuesday, and ended at 7,575.83 on Wednesday.
Share traders on both sides of the Atlantic are driving share prices higher in the belief that interest rates will not have to soon to choke off inflation.

London's FTSE index of blue-chip shares made a brief but unsuccessful attempt to break through the 4,800 level earlier, hitting a new trading high on the way, but then eased back and stood at 4,773.7, up 16.3 points at 1400 gmt.

Confirmation that PacifiCorp of the U.S. plans to buy Energy Group for $9.6 billion also lifted sentiment, though Energy shares were trading well below PacifiCorp's offer. They were up 2-1/2 pence to 650-1/2p.

The deal, said NatWest strategist David McBain, "will add more liquidity to already cash-rich corporate and institutional accounts." Liquidity, already at historically high levels, has been the driving force behind the British market rally, he added.

Another factor pushing continental market higher was abating fears about the future of European monetary union as France and Germany appeared ready to reach a compromise on a stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline after the start of the new currency in January 1999.

"There is more and more confidence out there that the euro will come on time, even if it's weaker than expected, so people now expect that money will keep coming into Europe after currency union," a trader said.

In Paris, the blue chip CAC share index rose to a trading high of 2,805.37 points, propelled by Wall Street and hopes of a ratification of a European stability pact at next week's EU Amsterdam summit, traders said. The CAC-40 index was up 28.51 points at 2,788.78 at 1400 GMT.
"There's a lot of volume out there," a broker said. He added that the message from the markets was that "in France, politics don't matter".
Germany's DAX index of leading shares ended 36.45 points higher at 3,744.44.

Meanwhile, the dollar took a breather after a week of wild swings, with traders looking for a cue from a summit of European Union countries starting on Monday and a Group of Seven leading industrial nations meeting later in the week.

U.S.-Japan relations came under the spotlight this week as traders drove the dollar down to a six-month low against the yen on Wednesday amid concern about trade friction between the two and then pushed it back up four percent in the next trading session as such worries ebbed.
They are now looking to next week's G7 summit in Denver for reassurance that trade tensions will remain at bay.

Dollar/mark has acted as a weathervane for hopes of an accord on a EU budget stability pact. Speculation that European economic and monetary union may be delayed was triggered after France on Monday asked for time to consider the pact and urged the adoption of measures to promote growth and employment.

EU officials dispelled such talk, saying the pact will be formally adopted at their Amsterdam summit Monday and Tuesday. This has dislodged the mark from the highs it set early in the week against other European and major currencies.
"People don't want to take any positions ahead of the EU and G7 summits," said Craig Justham, at Creditanstalt Bankverein.
Dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7305 at 1400 gmt, while dollar/yen was at 114.40.

Expectations grew that the U.S. will refrain from criticising a recent widening in Japan's trade surpluses at the G7 summit after U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Thursday that leaders will not pay special attention to U.S.-Japan trade flows.
Also, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said America will not use the dollar as an excessive instrument of trade policy.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7305 marks and 114.40 yen compared with 1.7265 marks and 113.99 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index finished was up 16.3 points at 4,773.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed was up 28.51 points at 2,,788.78.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 36.45 points at 3,744.44.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1400 GMT
Gold was fixed at $341.20 in the morning compared with $342.65 an ounce in late trade on Thursday.
